correctness.rationale: The exact graph potential gives the equal-current condition and constrained Hessian; any non-acute strong edge prevents positive definiteness by a two-edge witness. The stable winding-one family therefore reduces to a single scalar f_m(beta), which has a unique nondegenerate global minimum by the sign pattern of a tangent difference. The physical Hessian is positive for the smaller-beta solution and has one negative direction for the larger-beta solution. Reflection treats winding minus one. With 0<h<1/4, Hessian sign decides linear attraction since all eigenvalues of the weighted cycle Laplacian lie below 4. An implicit-function expansion yields the two terms of the threshold; finite numeric computations supplement the universal proof, not replace it.

value.rationale: An exactly weakened edge is a natural defect in a reciprocal phase ring; the critical strength is a nontrivial winding-protection threshold, not a normalization check or arbitrary slice. The all-n unique-fold theorem distinguishes one attracting and one one-unstable-direction branch, gives a precise loss-of-persistence mechanism, and supplies the leading 1/(n-1) and next cubic coefficients, useful in assessing multistability of finite defective oscillator rings. General cycle-flow methods predate the calculation and are credited.
